## Intent

The finding admits it is already in the public record: a prior audit, a documented design decision, a known issue. Submitting it signals that the prior audit was not read, which is worse than not submitting.

## Detection signals

Signals are admission phrases: "previously reported", "already known", "already been reported", "previously disclosed", "acknowledged as a known issue", "known issue", "documented as intended", "same root cause as", "accepted as <name> issue", or an issue id (H-1, M-01, L-3) sitting next to one of those admissions. A bare mention of "prior audit" is deliberately NOT a signal, because "the prior audit missed this" is the opposite claim. A bare issue id is not a signal either: drafts number their own findings. Firm names are not listed. "accepted as <name> issue" matches every venue without naming one, and a shipped rule that names one venue is a disclosure. The rule still fires only on the report's own words, which is why it cannot find the duplicate the report does not mention. That case is the index behind --index, not this rule. On the 0.6.0 public bench this rule fired zero times: judged writeups do not contain these admissions. Widening it to "prior audit" would kill the finding that says the prior audit missed the bug. That trade was checked and kept.

Patterns are case-insensitive regular expressions matched against the full text of the
draft finding, subject to the engine rules below.

**Fires when at least one of these matches:**

```text
  previously[- ](reported|identified|reviewed|raised|accepted|assessed|documented)
  already[- ](reported|known|acknowledged|accepted|covered|raised|identified|documented|assessed)
  known (issue|limitation|characteristic|design)
  (prior|earlier|previous|published) audit .{0,60}(covered|identified|accepted|reported|raised|documented)
  documented (as |)(intended|design)
  same root[- ]cause (as|with|behind|of)
  accepted as [^.]{0,80}(issue|finding|report)
  (duplicate of|same (issue|finding|bug|defect) as) [^.]{0,60}(issue|finding|report)
  already been (reported|identified|disclosed|documented|accepted|raised)
  previously disclosed
  acknowledged as (a )?(known|duplicate|prior)
  (accepted|duplicate|prior audit|prior report|same root[- ]cause|previously[- ]reported|contest issue|warden issue|published audit).{0,80}\b[chmliqs]-\d{1,3}\b
```

## Escape hatches

Suppression is sentence-scoped. "no prior audit of module A" does not hide "same root cause as issue M-1" in a later sentence. In the matching sentence, the negations are "no prior audit", "not covered by a prior review", "no known", "not previously", "new since", "first audit of", and a prior audit that missed the surface. The engine's negation window applies on top of those.

**Suppressed when any of these matches, in the same sentence as the fire:**

```text
  no prior audit
  not (covered|found|identified) (by|in) (a |any )?prior
  no (known|previously)
  not previously
  new since
  first (audit|review) of
  (prior|earlier|previous) audit .{0,40}(missed|did not cover|does not cover|never covered)
```

## Known false-positive modes

These are the shapes where the rule fires on something it should not. They are the
reason a firing is a prompt to check, not a verdict.

- A report that cites a prior audit to distinguish its own finding from it, where the distinguishing language is not one of the six negations.
- A finding about a *regression* that reintroduces a previously fixed issue.
- A report that quotes the program's known-issues list in order to argue the entry does not cover this case.

## Synthetic examples

Both examples are synthetic. They describe no real report and no real target.

**Fires:** "This was already reported in a prior audit and accepted as intended."

**Does not fire:** "No prior audit covers this module; the surface is new since the last review."

## Corrective action

Do not submit. Prior audit findings are part of the public record; submitting a known design characteristic signals you did not read the prior audit.

## Changelog

| Date | Change |
|---|---|
| 2026-11-09 | "already been reported", "previously disclosed", and "acknowledged as a known issue" were added. The 0.6.0 bench still showed zero fires; judged text does not admit these phrases. "prior audit" stays out. |
| 2026-11-09 | Same-root-cause admissions, "accepted as <name> issue", and issue ids next to an admission now fire. Hyphenated "previously-reported" fires. Suppression is sentence-scoped. Firm names stay out of the catalog. |
| 2026-10-08 | Escape hatches for negated forms added before the first catalog commit. The rule previously over-fired on findings whose whole point was that the surface was new. |
| 2026-10-10 | A bare "prior audit" removed as a signal. "The prior audit missed this" is the opposite claim and the old rule hard-killed it; the engine's negation window now applies on top of the explicit escape hatches. |
